content: 1. When co-administered with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat, careful dose titration of the antidepressant is necessary to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. This includes starting with the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitoring the response during co-administration. 2. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 5. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates, while this effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 7. Cobicistat and itraconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Specific dosage recommendations for itraconazole with cobicistat are not available. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor dose reduction is recommended when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 9. Cobicistat and ketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole with cobicistat are not available. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions to CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially necessitating dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 14. Cobicistat and levoketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole with cobicistat are not available. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraceptive use is recommended. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Due to lumacaftor's induction effect on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce lumateperone dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Methadone dose adjustment may be necessary. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust mifepristone dose based on the patient's current regimen. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Monitor for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nefazodone also increases cobicistat levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. No dosage adjustment is necessary. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dosage adjustment may be necessary. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Manage adverse effects with dose reduction or therapy discontinuation if needed. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust oliceridine dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel and paclitaxel protein-bound formulations by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paroxetine by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perphenazine by an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 50. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pravastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 54. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of protriptyline by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect.
